text:
The primary material of a candle is wax.

Wax is a combustible, hydrophobic substance that is solid at room temperature and melts when heated. It is typically derived from animal, vegetable, or mineral sources. Common types include paraffin wax (derived from petroleum), beeswax (produced by honey bees), soy wax (made from soybean oil), and stearin (often derived from animal fats or hydrogenated vegetable oils). The wax serves as the fuel source for the candle, drawn up the wick via capillary action where it vaporizes and combusts to produce light and heat.
